title: Analysis of the Hospital Node in the Management of Acute Events of Patients Referred to Pediatric Palliative Care
official: Analysis of the Hospital Node in the Management of Acute Events of Patients Referred to Pediatric Palliative Care
summary: This study aims to analyze the role of the hospital node in the acute event management of pediatric patients referred to Pediatric Palliative Care. Patients eligible for pediatric palliative care experience frequent hospitalizations. In oncology patients, hospitalizations are mainly for the treatment of the disease and the performance of diagnostic and/or therapeutic procedures, whereas in the case of non-oncology children, admissions occur particularly for the occurrence of complications, which may affect different organs and systems. Hospitalization times are on average longer, so much so that in some cases they can even exceed 100 consecutive days, and have a high risk of re-hospitalization.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Living patients aged \<18 years at the time of the event
* Patients with conditions eligible for PPCs according to Association for Children's Palliative Care/Royal College of Pediatrics and Child Health

Exclusion Criteria:

* NA
